suggested_policies.rationale: HLD_GCP_109 accepts both COS and COS_CONTAINERD. COS (Docker-based) was deprecated in GKE 1.24 and removed in GKE 1.29. Any node pool using COS on GKE 1.29+ will fail to provision. COS_CONTAINERD is the only valid container-runtime OS from GKE 1.29 onwards and should be enforced explicitly.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_002
name: GKE node pools must use COS_CONTAINERD image type
principle: supply-chain
severity: HIGH
rationale: |
  The COS image type uses the deprecated Docker container runtime and was removed
  from GKE in version 1.29. Node pools provisioned with image_type = "COS" on
  GKE 1.29+ will fail to create. COS_CONTAINERD uses containerd as the runtime,
  which is the supported standard. HLD_GCP_109 permits both values; this rule
  closes the gap by enforcing the current-generation image exclusively.
remediation: |
  Set image_type explicitly to COS_CONTAINERD:
  ```hcl
  resource "google_container_node_pool" "main" {
    node_config {
      image_type = "COS_CONTAINERD"
    }
  }
  ```
resources:
  google_container_node_pool:
    path: node_config.image_type
    equals: COS_CONTAINERD

suggested_policies.rationale: GKE Dataplane V2 (datapath_provider = ADVANCED_DATAPATH) replaces iptables with eBPF via Cilium, providing kernel-level NetworkPolicy enforcement, built-in network observability, and resistance to iptables bypass attacks. There is no existing holden policy requiring ADVANCED_DATAPATH and this setting is not enabled by default.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_003
name: GKE clusters should use GKE Dataplane V2 for eBPF-based network enforcement
principle: network-security
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  GKE Dataplane V2 uses eBPF via Cilium instead of iptables for NetworkPolicy
  enforcement. iptables-based enforcement can be bypassed under certain kernel
  conditions and provides no visibility into policy decisions. Dataplane V2 enforces
  NetworkPolicy in the kernel (bypassing userspace) and exposes per-flow network
  telemetry via the GKE Network Policy logging feature. It must be set at cluster
  creation time and cannot be changed afterward.
remediation: |
  Set datapath_provider in network_config at cluster creation:
  ```hcl
  resource "google_container_cluster" "main" {
    network_config {
      datapath_provider = "ADVANCED_DATAPATH"
    }
  }
  ```
resources:
  google_container_cluster:
    path: network_config.datapath_provider
    equals: ADVANCED_DATAPATH

suggested_policies.rationale: Node pool boot disks smaller than 50 GB can exhaust space under normal workloads due to container image layers, emptyDir volumes, and system logs. When a node disk fills, the kubelet enters a pressure state, evicts pods, and may become unable to pull new images. No existing holden policy enforces a minimum disk size for node pools.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_004
name: GKE node pool boot disks must be at least 50 GB
principle: reliability
severity: LOW
rationale: |
  GKE node boot disks store the OS, kubelet artifacts, container image layers,
  and emptyDir volumes. Disks smaller than 50 GB risk running out of space
  under typical workloads, triggering node-level disk pressure, pod evictions,
  and potential node Not-Ready states. The GCP default is 100 GB; teams that
  reduce this for cost savings often underestimate the space consumed by image
  layer caching.
remediation: |
  Set disk_size_gb to at least 50 in node_config:
  ```hcl
  resource "google_container_node_pool" "main" {
    node_config {
      disk_size_gb = 100
    }
  }
  ```
resources:
  google_container_node_pool:
    path: node_config.disk_size_gb
    gte: 50
